title: I'm bad at math, so I gave Claude one rule for my number puzzle: every board must be solvable
author: office-canard
selftext:
must be one has a rule you can get in about three seconds: combine neighboring numbers with +, -, x and / until every tile is a 1.



That's the whole game. No story, no characters, no ending.



How AI fit in: I gave Claude one rule. Every board has to be solvable, because that's a puzzle maker's basic courtesy to the player. I left the method entirely to Claude. What it came up with was building every board backwards, starting from all 1s, so a solution exists before you ever see the board.



\- 100 fixed stages. The numbers get bigger as you go, from single digits up to the 90s

\- After stage 100, new boards are generated in real time, forever

\- A hint button that shows you the next move



The honest part: I'm not good at math, so I don't find this one all that fun myself. I made it for people whose brains work with numbers much faster than mine does.



I'm a one-person studio, and this is one of 25 small games I've released so far. I'm curious: does a puzzle with zero story still pull you in, or do you need something more to keep playing?
